title: Server CPU semiconductor and buyer pricing economics: reproducible public-evidence estimators
scope: x86 Intel Xeon/AMD EPYC public reference pricing, Intel ASP disclosure, negotiated price identification limits, supplier strategy, OEM and enterprise procurement, workload TCO, implications for all-ISA server CPU silicon forecasting. No client/NDA screenshots, private information, or unsupported realized hyperscaler discounts.

search_before_write.dedupe_notes: Reuses D006 net CPU ASP, D003 architecture by buyer/workload, D007 shipment counts, and D009 cores/socket gaps. No preexisting pricing economics packet or canonical price series found; do not duplicate TAM/forecast series or infer AMD EPYC CPU revenue from combined Data Center revenue.

claims.statement: Intel attributed its FY2022 server ASP decline of 5% to a higher mix of hyperscale revenue.
Intel reported FY2023 server ASP growth of 20% driven by lower hyperscale mix and higher high-core-count mix.
Intel reported FY2024 server ASP growth of 11%, principally associated with increased high-core-count mix.
Intel reported FY2025 server ASP decline of 4%, including pricing actions and increased lower-core-count mix.
Intel reported server ASP growth of 48% in Q2 2026 and 38% YTD vs corresponding 2025 periods; premium mix was the majority driver; demand-based pricing was smaller.
Intel reported server volume growth of 9% Q2 and 2% YTD, mainly due to hyperscaler demand, and demand exceeding its available supply owing to internal constraints.
claims.source_locator: MD&A DCAI, adjacent paragraph to ASP explanation

claims.statement: AMD revenue-recognition disclosures include OEM/ODM rebates, distributor rebates, price protection, certain marketing programs and customer incentives; price list less invoice discount is not necessarily net realized semiconductor revenue.
AMD published an EPYC 9965 reference price of USD 14,813 per CPU on a 1,000-unit basis at its October 2024 launch.

relationships.counting_rule: One silicon shipment; CSP as end buyer, OEM/ODM as separate channel axis
No addition of OEM sale plus enterprise/hyperscaler end-buyer acquisition

signals.statement: Reported ASP and hyperscale customer mix moved in different directions across 2022 and 2026.
signals.inference: Buyer volume may have bargaining power but premium SKU mix and supply constraints can reverse aggregate ASP. A single universal hyperscaler discount is indefensible.
signals.alternative: Some matched-SKU net prices may have risen even faster than public aggregates; undisclosed mix prevents disentangling.

signals.statement: The EPYC 9965 2024 launch 1KU anchor offers a dated reference baseline; the current live SKU page is mutable.
signals.inference: Model lifecycle repricing separately from next-generation flagship public anchors; do not apply web-current price retroactively.
signals.alternative: Changing regional pages/price program and noncaptured timestamp could explain differences.

hypotheses.thesis: For a matched SKU and period, higher committed qualified purchase volume predicts lower manufacturer net realized price, but the conditional effect varies with supply scarcity and outside options.
hypotheses.alternative: Observed ASP gap mainly SKU and customer mix; constrained capacity, custom products and rebates change apparent discount.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Acquire legally publishable same-SKU/time buyer-class net-price samples with quantities and terms; test conditional volume effect, sample selection and temporal holdout.

hypotheses.thesis: OEM CPU upgrade option delta responds less than one-for-one or with lags to semiconductor reference repricing.
hypotheses.alternative: Bundled forced co-requisites and configurator merchandising fully explain observed spreads.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Capture matched baseline CPU options and BOM changes across OEMs/time; estimate pass-through with co-requisite controls and compare procurement awards.

methods.name: Reconcile five noninterchangeable price layers
inputs: invoice concessions and rebates if disclosed
methods.procedure: Classify and store reference, invoice/contract, net realized semiconductor, OEM embedded option/shadow, and buyer cost per validated unit of work. Net supplier realization = invoiced consideration minus revenue-reducing rebates/credits/price protection, not simply list minus nominal discount. Never infer undocumented components.
methods.output: Comparability-safe price layers with evidence-specific missing values
methods.identification_boundary: Actual hyperscaler net paid CPU prices are generally unobservable from published reference prices and enterprise server awards.

methods.name: Same-SKU reference repricing index
inputs: multiple dated public snapshots for identical SKU
same region, currency, tax and 1KU/RCP basis
methods.procedure: For each SKU with at least two comparable snapshots calculate log(P_t/P_t-1); form a weighted geometric index with explicitly chosen constant weights. Separately compute hedonic log(P_s,t) with SKU quality controls (cores, clocks, cache, TDP, channels, generation, positioning) for changing mix. Publish coverage and extrapolation intervals.
methods.output: Public reference price index; never net ASP

methods.name: Reported ASP versus mix and price decomposition
inputs: volume-weighted SKU and customer shares where known
methods.procedure: ASP_t = sum_{SKU,customer} shipment_share_t * net_unit_price_t. Separate SKU, generation, buyer-class, price/rebate and interaction changes using a symmetric Shapley attribution only where joint weights and prices are identified. Where weights absent report underidentified and scenario ranges, not a causal share split.
methods.output: Aggregate movement bridge and explicitly nonidentified components

methods.name: Configured-server CPU option-delta proxy
inputs: identical OEM server model, baseline, geography, date, tax status
methods.procedure: Record raw option delta; replay matched configuration and subtract priced required co-requisites if observable; collect repeated variants across SKUs/dates and test cross-model reference-price changes versus adjusted OEM spreads. Treat OEM delta as channel shadow price, not supplier transaction cost.
methods.output: OEM adjusted CPU-option shadow spread and pass-through coefficient with interval

methods.name: Buyer-class net-price model with nonidentification gate
inputs: same SKU/date net semiconductor contract observations
terms, region, channel, customer class, product age
methods.procedure: Only when comparable net transaction observations exist, estimate log(net_price/reference) on customer class, volume, SKU/date fixed effects, geography and terms; use hierarchical shrinkage if sparse, and leave-one-buyer-out validation. Otherwise declare exact hyperscaler vs enterprise discount unidentified and provide clearly synthetic range sensitivities.
methods.output: Conditional buyer-class net price gap if identified; otherwise null with missing_reason

methods.name: Buyer workload 3–5-year cost-per-work unit
inputs: server prices, RAM/storage/network, software licensing, power and PUE, utilization
methods.procedure: For each competing validated topology calculate TCO = acquisition + paid license + support + rack/facility + energy + deployment - residual; work = successful validated tasks or SLA-qualified throughput*runtime; rank by TCO/work. Solve break-even CPU discount needed to flip ranking and Monte Carlo correlated power/utilization/performance/license scenarios.
methods.output: Break-even procurement price, TCO/work, sensitivity bands

methods.name: Evidence-to-DB reproducibility contract
inputs: source URL, publisher, filing/version, locator, as_of/capture timestamp, region and unit
raw original or rights-compatible cryptographic digest
methods.procedure: Keep immutable source snapshots when permitted; normalize FX by ECB as-of date, taxes separately, canonical SKU, seller/buyer channel, market boundary and price layer. Preserve no-quote and unknown values as null+reason. Quarterly refresh, audit sampled extraction, holdout backtests, filing reconciliation and independent cross-channel checks. Stage packets before any database seed promotion.
methods.output: Versioned provenance record and evidence grading; no overwrite of vintages

requirements.name: Public CPU pricing observatory ingestion and quality gates
requirements.user_outcome: Compare observed reference price trends, vendor reported ASP, OEM option shadow price, inferred net transaction bounds and TCO without confusing market boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Each observed price has SKU/region/currency/quantity basis/snapshot timestamp/price_layer/source evidence
Unknown negotiated prices render missing/unidentifiable, not zero or made-up discount
Store yearly and quarterly reported ASP indices in separate comparable series
No promotion until reviewed source locators and automated research checks pass
Separate observed, sourced vendor assertions, modeled and scenarios in UI

promotions.decision_note: Staged only; review series metric ID, FY vs CY accounting and canonical row uniqueness before promotion.
Staged only; separate half-year YoY metric, never chain with annual ASP index.
A per-SKU 1KU reference belongs in future price_snapshots table, not macro server CPU shipments/revenue actuals.
Methodology is a research design, not verified observed data; linked technical design published separately.

handoff.summary: Multi-route 2026 pricing intake anchored to public Intel ASP disclosures, AMD 1KU launch prices, OEM configurator and public procurement source classes. No transaction-level semiconductor prices established. Implementation design, no production seed or dashboard changes.
